subject: Keep sds lengths in size_t when comparing and caching keys (#5133)
reason: The change only alters behaviour when an sds object's byte length reaches 2^31 (2 GiB): dictSdsKeyCompare and evictionPoolPopulate held the length in a signed int that overflows to a negative value for a >=2GiB key/member, so memcmp/memcpy receive a sign-extended huge size_t and crash or mis-compare; keeping the length in size_t fixes it. For any length below 2^31 the int and size_t code are bit-for-bit identical, so nothing smaller can distinguish the two builds. Reaching the changed path requires literally sending a 2 GiB key name or set member (that is why the upstream tests are tagged larg
